newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GOVT BODY APPROVES 1996 NBP MONETARY POLICY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GOVT BODY APPROVES 1996 NBP MONETARY POLICY.

text.p: The Polish government's economic committee (KERM) approved on Monday the National Bank of Poland's report on the realisation of its monetary policy in 1996, the government press office said in a statement.

The KERM noted that in the first months of last year the NBP had to curb the fast growth of official currency reserves, while towards the end of the year the central bank had to diminish domestic demand, mainly through high interest rates.
Non-financial sector deposits in the banking system rose to 87.9 billion zlotys last year, above the upper limit of 87.3 billion envisaged in the policy outline, the statement said.
Credit for the sector also grew dynamically at 35.2 percent for corporates and 107.8 percent for households.
The Polish central bank is independent and the approval of its report by the government is a formality.
